perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He works with Patricia Ndiaye at a community bank, where he sometimes helps with maintenance and repairs.
- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn and down than usual during recent shifts, and remembered her as usually vibrant.
- He asked if she was okay. She said it was “nothing really,” just personal stuff, and thanked him for asking.
- He offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk. She said she appreciated it and that it meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He told her he’d been reading about financial planning strategies and offered to discuss them. She said that could be helpful and that she’d been overwhelmed with bills.
- He offered to look over budgeting tips together when she felt up to it. She thanked him and said she’d take him up on it soon.
- After that, he worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances, so he clarified that he only wanted to help, not pry. Patricia said she didn’t see it as prying and was grateful for the offer.
- He told her he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend. She said she appreciated having someone to turn to.
- Later, he asked how she was doing and about weekend plans. She said she was good and planned a quiet weekend at home. He said he’d probably relax and read, and reminded her she could reach out if she needed anything. She thanked him.
- He continued checking in on her at work. She said she was busy but handling it, thanked him for checking in, and said it was great to have his support. He responded that they were all there to help each other.
